lines.L03: A photometer shines one wavelength through the cuvette.
lines.L04: Absorbance compares the light going in with the light coming out: A = log₁₀(I₀/I).
lines.L05: At absorbance 1, only ten percent of the light gets through; at 2, one percent.
lines.L06: Within a range, absorbance rises in proportion to concentration: the Beer–Lambert law.
lines.L07: Past the linearity limit, the curve bends: readings fall short.
lines.L08: Three cuvettes: the blank sets zero, then standard, then sample.
lines.L09: Concentration = A sample ÷ A standard × C standard.
lines.L10: Above the limit? Dilute, measure again, and multiply by the dilution factor.
lines.L11: LabGuide’s Lecture mode has a protocol on photometry basics.
lines.L12: Blank, standard and sample, step by step — and the calculation…
lines.L13: …plus the rule for results above the linearity limit.
lines.L14: Wavelength, blank and limits always come from your reagent’s IFU.
lines.L15: LabGuide — Learn → Lecture mode → Practical protocols.
